objective: Harden the Windows visible Hermes worker console so accidental mouse text-selection / QuickEdit mode cannot pause a live worker or defeat apparent watchdog progress. Preserve visible streaming while preventing console-selection freezes, and add regression/evidence for the launch behavior.
allowed_scope: Inspect remote_queue/visible_worker.py and the Windows console launch path.

Implement the smallest safe Windows-specific hardening that prevents QuickEdit/selection from suspending worker progress while preserving the visible terminal requirement. Prefer explicitly disabling ENABLE_QUICK_EDIT_MODE on the worker console or an equivalent supported console-mode change; do not hide the worker window.
Do not broadly change unrelated terminal settings or the owner's global Windows Terminal/PowerShell preferences.
Add isolated tests where practical and record exact verification/evidence.
Do not mutate any running task contract; commit/push recoverably.
stop_conditions: Do not kill unrelated processes or modify global console settings destructively.
Do not expose secrets or weaken the worker watchdog/timeouts.
If Windows console behavior cannot be changed safely per-process, record the exact limitation and leave current behavior unchanged.
notes: Triggered by an observed live worker window whose title showed 'Select Administrator: Hermes Remote Worker ...' while output appeared frozen beyond the nominal 300s idle watchdog. In classic Windows console, Select/QuickEdit mode can pause console application progress. The active E3 gate had already landed commit 91a2adc2 while the visible wrapper remained open, consistent with a finalization/console interaction stall. This task should prevent recurrence without sacrificing visible worker output.
